comments.text: I bought my first home in 1990. It was 45k dollars. Our payment was 465 a month. For 30yrs.  I think the interest rate was like 11-12 percent. It wasn’t necessarily affordable, since my income was about 1000. A month.  Then my husband and I divorced, I couldn’t make that payment by myself, so I had a roommate. I had a car payment, I think it was 181.00, then insurance, and let’s talk utilities, and home repairs. Gas, food.  I barely had anything left, like Pennie’s.  Two yrs later and a couple roommates later, I met and married my husband of 22yrs. We sold our home, moved to Phoenix, bought another house, 89k, 14%,  our payment was 1200.00 a month.  We had 80dollars left every two weeks, that covered food and gas. We had credit cards and minimum payments when the AC died.  We hobbled thru it. Finally he got an outside job with phone company, and our money finally balanced out. Point is here, nothing in this life is affordable, NOTHING!!. When we bought our last house in oregon,  that was 200k, and the interest was 11%!!.  However, as the rates dropped two points sometimes three we would refi, take a small chunk of equity out at same time, paid of our vehicles, added a deck, bought some new appliances, and saved the rest.  Was any of that affordable at the time?? NO!! It’s always been a pinch. But! We did it!  My husband passed, 12yrs ago., he had blessed me with life insurance, what little was left on the house I paid it off. Lived there 22yrs. What we paid 200k for was now selling at 550k.  I sold it five years later and downsized to this place, that I paid cash for.  So I can live on my SS, barely, but I’m doing it.  Life seldom is affordable.
